name: The Mughal Age: Domes, Dynasties and the Company
description: Sultans, emperors and merchants: how India passed from Delhi's sultans to the Mughal court and the Taj Mahal, and then to the East India Company and the Raj.

checkpoints.name: Sultans and kingdoms
checkpoints.note: The Delhi Sultanate ruled much of the north, while Vijayanagara and its capital Hampi stood in the south. Guru Nanak taught the faith that became Sikhism, and Vasco da Gama's ships reached India by sea in 1498.

checkpoints.name: The empire of Akbar
checkpoints.note: The Mughal Empire began in 1526. Akbar enlarged it, built the city of Fatehpur Sikri, and the Sikhs' Golden Temple at Amritsar dates from these years. In 1600 the English East India Company was founded.

checkpoints.name: The age of the Taj
checkpoints.note: Shah Jahan ruled in the empire's richest days and built the Taj Mahal in memory of his wife. Afterwards the Mughal emperors lost real power, and rival states and trading companies grew stronger.

checkpoints.name: The Company takes control
checkpoints.note: After the Battle of Plassey in 1757 the East India Company became a ruling power, known as Company rule in India. In 1857 the Indian Rebellion shook it, and the Company's rule ended soon after.

checkpoints.name: The Raj and independence
checkpoints.note: The Crown took over and the British Raj began. The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885, Mahatma Gandhi led mass campaigns, and in 1947 the Partition of India created India and Pakistan.
